summary: 1849 brick light at the mouth of the Maurice River on Delaware Bay: custodians from 1911, discontinued 1941, relit 1980, state land and set to reopen in October 2026.

lens.where: Sixth-order Fresnel installed 1856 (LighthouseFriends); the lantern now holds a 250 mm optic (USLHS)

structures.note: Whitewashed brick; 39 ft tower on a square keeper's dwelling (USLHS); focal height 48 ft
Built 1900 to 1901 (NRHP); erection begun under contract by the 1900 Board report

staffing.note: Acetylene light fitted in 1911; keepers replaced by custodians paid $1 a year (LighthouseFriends)

access.note: State land; reopening on a limited basis was set for 16 Oct 2026 (Inquirer). Closure years differ between sources (2021 and 2024).

facts.agency: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (state land); Cumberland County to lease the lighthouse from 2026

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Our sources agree the light is an active aid to navigation: the NRHP says the Coast Guard relit it in 1980 and it 'faithfully remains' an active aid, and the Inquirer in 2026 reports it remains one. The closures were to visitors, not to the light.

Sources differ on when the lighthouse last closed. LighthouseFriends gives March 2021 (reopened August 2021 under a temporary license, and the society left in September 2024). The Inquirer gives 2024. Not resolved here.

LighthouseFriends gives 1955 for the rescinded federal auction and transfer to New Jersey. The NRHP nomination gives 10 April 1956 as the date the vacant property was deeded to the state. Both are stated in the story; not resolved.

The Inquirer (2026) says the society installed period-replica pieces in various rooms, and that those have been removed. LighthouseFriends (2017) describes five rooms furnished with period antiques. Not resolved.

notes_for_editor: ROSTER: 13 USLHS lines, 1849 to 1914 (Principal Lighthouse Keeper and Custodian headings). The last custodian line is open-ended (Joseph M. Scull, 'at least 1913-'); LighthouseFriends says the last custodian left in 1945. Not reconciled; the story gives the LighthouseFriends date. PERSON SLUGS are attached: this USLHS record is this station (East Point (Maurice River), est. 1849, Maurice River lighthouse alias). RANGE LIGHTS: the 1897-1898 Maurice River range lights are separate structures (USLHS 'Maurice River Range Front' and 'Maurice River Range Rear' are other records); not used as this station. The 1899 red-sector entry is cited to the 'Maurice River light-station' (the older tower), which the 1899 list names alongside the separate 'Maurice River range light-station'. CLOSURE: LighthouseFriends gives March 2021 (closure and reopening) and September 2024 (society vacated); the Inquirer gives 2024. DEED DATE: NRHP gives 10 April 1956; LighthouseFriends gives 1955 for the transfer. PERIOD ROOMS: Inquirer says replicas, removed; LighthouseFriends (2017) says antiques. REOPENING: the Inquirer (9 Oct 2026) says reopening on a limited basis on 16 Oct 2026; whether it happened is not verified. DEP RELEASE: dep.nj.gov/newsrel/26_0046 returned no text when fetched, so the story relies on the Inquirer. FOCAL HEIGHT: NRHP says about 45 ft; LighthouseFriends' 1878 description says 48 ft; the record's 14.6 m is 48 ft. LENS DATE: the 1856 Fresnel is from LighthouseFriends only; NRHP does not date the lens. WWII: the mayor quoted in the Inquirer says the light was darkened so U-boats could not use it; not used, as no source here gives that reason. STORMS: no storm, wreck or rescue tied to the light was found in the sources read. SCAN PAGES: the 1895 (entry 'Maurice River range lights') and 1896-97 (entries 437 and 438) Board volumes have no page index in the corpus, and the in-item search returned no hit, so their scan pages could not be confirmed. The story cites the entry and the volume for those two footnotes. The 1899 (scan 20, 23), 1900 (scan 102) and 1899 red-sector entries were checked. LighthouseFriends is copyrighted: paraphrased, with short quotations only. Confidence medium.
